papers.title_en: Dynamic Conflict Clustering with Lightweight Learning and Strategic Repair for Distributed Constraint Satisfaction
papers.evidence: 具结构化多智能体协调的修复式分布式约束求解器
papers.tldr: 分布式约束满足问题中，现有求解器依赖广泛重复通信且偏反应式，难兼顾效率与硬实例鲁棒性。DCC-Incomplete将未解部分划为冲突簇，用协调层限制通信，并引入记忆引导重启进行策略性修复与轻量学习。在图着色基准上，成功率由37.50%升至61.11%，中位运行时间由0.565s降至0.367s，每约束中位通信由12.493降至6.503条消息。结果表明动态冲突聚类与轻量学习修复能提升不完全DCSP求解的通信效率和鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: Distributed Constraint Satisfaction Problems (DCSPs) model distributed decision-making in multi-agent systems, where agents assign values to local variables while satisfying shared constraints. However, many DCSP solvers still rely on broad, repeated peer-to-peer communication and are largely reactive, with limited support for strategic coordination or learning. This increases communication overhead, can lead to stagnation, and reduces the success of hard instances. Hence, we propose Dynamic Conflict Clustering-Incomplete (DCC-Incomplete), a repair-based solver that combines conflict-centred decomposition, structured coordination, strategic repair, and lightweight learning for stagnation recovery. DCC-Incomplete groups the unsolved part of the problem into conflict clusters and restricts communication via a coordination layer to agents within the same conflict region. It also introduces memory-guided restart, enabling agents and clusters to pause, revise, and adapt repairs based on neighbouring conflict states. A thorough evaluation of DCC-Incomplete on distributed graph-colouring benchmarks with planted satisfying assignments shows that its memory-guided restart improves the success rate from 37.50% to 61.11%, reduces median runtime from 0.565s to 0.367s, and cuts median communication from 12.493 to 6.503 messages per constraint. These results suggest that dynamic conflict clustering, combined with lightweight strategic and learning-guided repair, improves both communication efficiency and robustness in incomplete DCSP solving.

papers.title_en: Collective Learning for Unified Robotic Manipulation via Predictive Dynamics Adaptation
papers.authors: Shaocheng Liu, Yuan Meng, Zhenshan Bing, Alois Knoll
papers.evidence: 跨本体统一操作策略的多机器人集体学习
papers.tldr: 跨不同机器人本体学习统一的笛卡尔操作策略时，由于各本体的转移动力学不同，简单聚合多机器人经验会把不兼容的动作模式平均化，导致策略歧义与性能崩溃。为此提出两阶段集体学习框架PACE：第一阶段用离线轨迹预训练表示层，从集体数据中提取任务级上下文；第二阶段引入带预测动力学适配器的决策层，通过让隐状态预测未来转移来约束策略，使其贴合执行机器人的动力学，同时保持实时推理、无需在线规划。仿真中总体成功率超过93%，在动力学分布外的零样本机器人上达到89%，优于Transformer行为克隆（82%）和扩散策略（66%），并在KUKA真机上验证了零样本仿真到现实迁移的可行性。
papers.abstract_en: Learning a collective policy for state-based Cartesian manipulation across diverse robotic embodiments presents a fundamental challenge due to embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. Collective learning aggregates multi-robot experience to discover shared task structure, yet naive aggregation can average incompatible action modes when different embodiments realize the same Cartesian command through different transition behavior. This leads to strategy ambiguity and performance collapse on dynamically outlying embodiments. To address this, we propose PACE, a two-stage collective learning framework that separates shared task-space intent from embodiment-dependent transition dynamics. The first stage employs a representation layer pre-trained on offline trajectories to extract task-level context from collective data. The second stage introduces a decision layer equipped with a predictive dynamics adapter. By forcing the latent state to predict future transitions, this adapter acts as a latent regularizer that grounds the policy in the transition behavior of the executing robot while preserving real-time inference without online planning. Evaluations across simulated embodiments demonstrate that our method prevents performance collapse on distinct robots. It achieves over 93\% overall success and 89\% on dynamically out-of-distribution zero-shot simulated robots, outperforming the Transformer behavior cloning (82\%) and diffusion policy baselines (66\%). Physical KUKA deployment further validates the feasibility of the full state-based pipeline under zero-shot sim-to-real transfer.

papers.title_en: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
papers.authors: Chenyuan Zhou, Yining Hong, Huang Huang, Yunfan Jiang, Wenlong Huang, David Held, Vitor Campagnolo Guizilini, Yue Wang, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Leonidas Guibas, Yejin Choi
papers.evidence: 可学习环境隐变量条件化机器人世界模型预测
papers.tldr: 机器人世界模型需推断摩擦、质量及环境规则等不可直接观测因素。T2-Z为世界模型引入可学习环境潜变量，训练时交替优化世界模型与环境潜变量，测试时冻结模型并从交互中优化新潜变量以适配未知环境。在7个仿真设置和4个真实任务中，物体预测误差从15.20降至7.00，动作成功率从33.73%升至72.96%。该方法表明测试时潜变量优化可高效适应新环境并形成结构化环境表征。
papers.abstract_en: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.
